turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she must not think such things, that she would live and be well again, and that he would not let her go without him.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told the eldest son that he must hurry and find a wife, for his mother was not well and he must have a son to carry on the family name, so that his mother could die in peace.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: the eldest son told his mother that he would do as she wished, and that he would start looking for a wife right away, so that she could rest easy.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked the eldest son to be patient and to find a wife who would be a good mother to his children, one who would teach them the ways of the family.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother that he would find a good wife who would make her proud, and that he would bring her to live with them on the farm, so she could see her grandchildren grow up.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told the maid that she must prepare a special meal for the eldest son, one that would show him her love and care.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: the maid asked O-lan, with a hesitant glance, if she might also help to prepare the eldest son's room for his future wife, so that everything would be ready for her arrival.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked the eldest son to tell her when he had decided on a wife, so that she could start making preparations for her arrival.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan should not worry about preparations for the eldest son's wife, that he would take care of it all and that she should focus on getting well.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan looked at Wang Lung with a determined expression, her eyes clouded with concern, and told him that she would not rest easy until the eldest son was married and settled.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan should not worry about the eldest son's wife, that she should focus on getting well and he would take care of everything.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan looked at Wang Lung with a determined expression, her eyes clouded with concern, and told him that his brother's wife-to-be would soon be arriving and needed a warm bath prepared.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung scolded O-lan, telling her that she was not to worry about the preparations, that he would see to it that everything was done, and that she should think only of her own recovery.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan insisted that Wang Lung must go to the village and bring back the wife-to-be, so that the preparations for the wedding could begin.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung scolded O-lan, telling her that she was being foolish and exhausting herself with such thoughts, and that he would not permit her to wear herself out before she was well.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: She asked the maid to help her sit up, so that she could see her eldest son's wife-to-be, and to bring her a bowl of warm water for her hands.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told O-lan that she would go immediately to prepare the warm water and help her sit up, and asked if there was anything else she could do for her.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that he must not worry about her, for she was thinking only of their son's happiness and the family's future.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung insisted that the preparations for the wedding would have to wait until O-lan was well enough to oversee them, and that he would not have their son's happiness ruined by his mother's exhausting herself.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was not worried about her own health, but about the future of their son and his wife-to-be, and that she wanted to see them settled before she passed away

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing she had to attend to before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan should not speak of dying and that it would please him if she did not.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan replied that she had to die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wedded this good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served O-lan, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe O-lan's face when she sweated in pain. Now O-lan wanted her son to come home, because she had to die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she might die easily, knowing that her grandson was stirred into life and a great-grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they had said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan declared that she would see Wang Lung wedded and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan instructed Wang Lung to sit there and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked if everyone had wine, if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot, if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it, and if the eight fruits were present.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was now content and that this thing in her may do as it would. She instructed her son to look to his father and his grandfather, and her daughter to look to her husband and his father and his grandfather and the poor fool in the court, there she was. And she told Wang Lung that he had no duty to any other.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan said that, even if she was ugly, she had borne a son; although she was but a slave, there was a son in her house.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan insisted that no one else could feed Wang Lung's son and care for him as she did. She told Wang Lung that beauty would not bear a man sons.
